html:
The Puri are an Indigenous people of southeast Brazil, from the Paraíba do Sul valley across parts of Rio de Janeiro, Minas Gerais, Espírito Santo and São Paulo. Their language, of the Purian family, is no longer spoken.

They lived in the Atlantic forest inland from the coast held by the Tupinambá, hunting, fishing, gathering and keeping small gardens. The colonists of Portuguese Brazil long left the hills alone, but the gold rush in Minas Gerais and then the spread of coffee plantations in the 1800s took their land. Many Puri died of disease or were forced into villages and labour, and by the late 1800s they were said to have vanished. In recent decades, families of Puri descent have organised to claim the name and revive the language. Nearby peoples included the Maxakali and the Pataxó.
